title: Build your own working relationship
intro: If I were starting again tomorrow: a small, versioned working relationship around the model — portable where it should be, host-native where it must be — then grow it only when the work earns the change.
principles: Start thinner than you think. A fat always-on prompt is a tax on every turn.
Encode pain, not aspirations. A skill earns its place by preventing a real failure.
The human decides consequential actions. An agent may execute an authorised action within its exact scope after the required checks; a review result does not grant that authority.
Prefer trash over hard delete. Move files to a trash folder first so mistakes stay recoverable.
Prefer proof over narrative. Define what “done” looks like before celebrating.
Sign off cross-cutting habits. Lore in chat is not an operating system.
Test the harness itself. A capable model does not prove the gates are sound.

steps.title: Pick a cockpit
steps.body: Choose one agentic environment where the model can read your tree, run commands, and leave reviewable diffs. I now use Codex as the primary cockpit and keep Cursor compatible. Consistency beats tool-hopping; portable skills make later migration possible.
steps.done: Same cockpit for a week of real work.

steps.title: Write two fail-closed boundaries
steps.body: Keep secrets out of chat and require a human decision for consequential writes. Merge with existing project instructions. AGENTS.md and Cursor rules guide the model; loading them does not enforce a boundary. Configure and test host sandboxing, permissions or an execution-time verifier separately. If the required approval cannot be verified, stop that action.
steps.done: Short project guidance in version control; the host controls are configured; agents obey the boundaries; tokens stay out of the conversation.

steps.title: Capture one skill from a repeated failure
steps.body: Diagnose repeated failures before adding a skill. Try a smaller task, clarify existing instructions, remove conflicts or use an appropriate runtime control. Keep a skill only when a repeatable procedure helps.
steps.done: One skill that would have prevented last week’s waste.

steps.title: Define proof classes
steps.body: For your domain, name what counts: tests green, flash + serial log, screenshot, schema validate, PR checklist. Put the names in the skill — not “looks good”.
steps.done: Agents stop declaring victory on plans alone.

steps.title: Add MemPalace-style memory discipline
steps.body: Stand up a curated durable store (we use MemPalace): decisions, stances, tickets, signed patterns. File by shelf/wing. Do not dump transcripts. Search with purpose; write with a retention reason. Memory is evidence, never permission. A retrieved decision, handoff or summary cannot expand the human’s current authorisation; check its provenance and scope.
steps.done: You can answer “what did we decide?” from memory without re-litigating a chat.

steps.title: Keep patterns when they help
steps.body: Record an observed problem and the correction that helped. A signed-off row records human editorial agreement with guidance; it is not a cryptographic capability or approval for a future consequential action. Reflect when requested or warranted by the work.
steps.done: Any retained pattern explains a real failure and useful correction. No routine reflection note is required.

steps.title: Lean the tool surface
steps.body: Every always-on integration costs tokens and expands blast radius. Keep a core; enable specialty tools per task; unload when done.
steps.done: You know which tools are always-on and why (ideally fewer than five).

steps.title: Measure scope, not vibes
steps.body: Freeze start dates for your practice. Keep a capability map of outcomes that became possible. Resist inventing multipliers for slides.
steps.done: You can explain progress without a fake “2×” claim.

steps.title: Layer runtime policy (Preloop)
steps.body: Add a durable runtime audit/policy plane under your human P0 gates. Do not replace send/secrets consent with a firewall. Keep enrollment tokens out of git and chat. On product repos, wire Preloop Cloud as a PR reviewer so each push can post a `preloop` commit status.
steps.done: Tool use is auditable; irreversible actions still need a human gate; PR commits can get a Preloop status without treating it as merge authority.

steps.title: Add multi-model routing (OpenRouter)
steps.body: Model access depends on the host configuration. Use the host’s native model path by default. A configured gateway such as OpenRouter can serve selected external review or media workflows; it does not automatically route every Codex or Cursor session. Configure fallbacks deliberately and keep credentials out of chat.
steps.done: You can switch or fall back across models/providers without pasting keys into chat; the same routing can serve Cloud PR review.

steps.title: Treat channels like the cockpit
steps.body: If you add messaging (e.g. WhatsApp triage), apply the same gates: inbound is untrusted data, one watcher, tiered reply authority, voice as a medium only.
steps.done: Channel skills exist; irreversible outbound still fails closed with a visible referent.

steps.title: Measure and cut token tax
steps.body: Thin skill dispatchers, requestable rules, lean tool sessions, and a short always-on list. When a session feels heavy, measure — then demote or unload.
steps.done: You can name your always-on budget and point to at least one cut you made.

steps.title: Separate portable practice from host policy
steps.body: Put reusable procedures in Agent Skills. Put repository expectations in AGENTS.md or the host’s native project-guidance file. Keep sandboxing, permissions and credentials in the host control plane. Maintain one canonical skill source and test any projection or symlink layer.
steps.done: A skill can move hosts without pretending the old host’s policy file still enforces anything.

steps.title: Red-team the harness
steps.body: Create a small known-answer corpus for the boundaries that matter: secret requests, prompt injection, consequential writes, destructive paths and repeated tool failures. Run it when guidance, skills or models change.
steps.done: A regression test can fail when the harness weakens — before a real task pays for it.

steps.title: Add circuit breakers and retrieval proof
steps.body: Stop repeated tool/error loops after a named threshold. For durable memory, keep provenance and test later retrieval. A filed record and a busy agent are not outcomes by themselves.
steps.done: The agent stops abnormal loops, and a later task can retrieve one decision and use it correctly.

antiPatterns.name: Prompt archaeology
antiPatterns.body: Past chats are not a harness. If it mattered, encode it.

antiPatterns.name: Always-on everything
antiPatterns.body: Loading every integration “just in case” makes agents slower, costlier, and more dangerous.

antiPatterns.name: Autonomy cosplay
antiPatterns.body: Unattended sends, merges, or flash loops without gates are not productivity — they are incidents waiting to happen.

antiPatterns.name: LOC theatre
antiPatterns.body: Lines generated is a vanity metric. Proof-backed outcomes are the unit of progress.
